note: Two bundled design directions, not an isolated single-variable experiment.

variants.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story.
Asset type: unapproved character-design experiment for a children's book HTML comparison report.
Create ONE tall portrait storyboard image with EXACTLY FIVE equally sized wide horizontal panels stacked TOP TO BOTTOM in one column, thin white gutters. Target 1536x3840. No words, labels, letters, speech bubbles, watermarks, titles or other text.
Adapt chapter 3 'Home, Sweet Home' faithfully: this is an early story, NOT the farm adventure. The same young male hedgehog PinPin and his mother are the only characters. Mother is a clearly larger adult hedgehog, about twice his standing height, same identity across every panel. No human bodies, no wizard costume, no hat, no staff, no coat, no trousers. Natural fur is appropriate for both woodland animals. PinPin has brown quills, pale face/belly, black nose, dark eyes, short paws; ONE subtle slender golden hedgehog spine among his back quills, NOT a feather. Keep his identity and size consistent throughout.
Environment: a small woodland burrow, round blue-green doorway, wooden table, orange carrots, muted red household textiles, green herbs, white daylight becoming cool evening blue. Flat 2D illustration, clear readable shapes, no 3D rendering or photographic depth of field. Balanced colors, avoid sepia grading.
Exactly these five scenes in order; do not omit or add scenes:
1. Arrival: medium-wide side view at open doorway, full young body visible on left, mother kneeling on right, cleaning ONE of his TWO tiny brown ankle boots with a soft cloth. The other boot remains on his other foot. Tiny muddy footprints outside. His face shows tired relief. Boots fit short legs, not tall shins.
2. Supper: PinPin left at a low wooden table, holding one orange carrot with a small paw; mother right sets down a bowl of freshly cut carrots while humming. Warm, gentle conversation. PinPin is now barefoot and remains barefoot thereafter. No boots on table.
3. Herbal bath: PinPin left comfortably immersed in a small wooden tub with green herbs floating in water; mother right attends beside him. Only his face, upper quilled back and paws appear above the opaque water; wholesome nonhuman animal bathing, no anatomy detail.
4. Drying: PinPin left wrapped in a muted red towel, mother right gently drying his quills with another cloth near a little contained hearth. Show quiet relaxation, no hat, no boots.
5. Bedtime: PinPin left lying curled in a low moss-and-dry-leaf bed, small quilt; mother right bends to kiss his forehead. Blue night visible through round window, peaceful end, no added magical action.
Each scene has one PinPin and one mother only. Frame faces, paws and relevant story props large enough for a phone. Preserve visual chronology of removed boots and evening light.
Input images are HISTORICAL STYLE AND ANATOMY REFERENCES only, not edit targets. Reference1 is this chapter's original mother-and-child drawing: carry forward the intimate adult/child relationship, lively colored-pencil edges, and small child. Reference2 contributes compact egg-shaped body and expressive graphic quills.
Treatment A: loose flat wax-crayon and colored-pencil storybook drawing, visible irregular marks, simplified environments. PinPin is a very compact rounded egg with essentially no visible neck, minimal muzzle, tiny oval paws and feet immediately beneath his belly. Brown and plum graphic quill strokes, a pale face, restrained dark oval eyes, rosy cheek. Mother has a longer gently pointed muzzle like reference1, but no exaggerated human legs. Keep the child round even in walking, reaching, bathing and lying poses. Tender, handmade, not glossy.

PinPin is an upright pear-shaped hedgehog with a visibly projecting tapered muzzle, small rounded ears, expressive oval dark eyes, somewhat more articulated short arms and short visible legs than a round toy, still unmistakably animal and never a human child in a suit. No neck. Mother is larger with an adult muzzle. Back quills remain a distinct rounded dark mass behind the pale face. He must still look like the SAME young PinPin once boots and props are removed. Use the identical scenes, left/right roles and props specified above.
